=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- scripts/unblock_actions.py:213-215, 352-356 | severity=high | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: The trailing group `(?:\s.*)?$` in FIXUP_DELIVERED_AFFECTED_ENTRY_RE accepts any text after the first backticked path, but fixup_delivered_body records only that first path, so a multi-path bullet such as "- o/r: `a.sh` and `b.sh`" counts as parsed while every later path, or another repository's entry, is silently dropped.
  WHY: The `grep -Fxq` coverage loop in unblock_fixup_delivered_close then passes when the fix-up PR changed only the first file, so the judge closes the issue as completed before the fix is complete; this breaks the docstring promise that an unread line never lets a partial fix close the issue (all reviewers rated it MAJOR; the suggested fix is `(?:\s[^`]*)?$` plus a skip test case).
- scripts/unblock_judge.sh:548-558 | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna]
  PROBLEM: The merged-PR lookup filters on `head="${owner}:ai/issue-${fixup}"` and re-checks only `.head.ref`, never `.head.repo.full_name == "${REPOSITORY}"`, so a same-named branch from another repository under the same owner can be accepted as the fix-up PR.
  WHY: If such a PR merged and changed the listed paths, the judge would post the close comment and PATCH the heal issue closed (all three flagging reviewers rated it MAJOR; anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 and z-ai_glm-5_3-flash rejected this finding in pass-1 because the call is scoped to `repos/${REPOSITORY}/pulls`).
- scripts/unblock_judge.sh:1834-1840 | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: After the close, `unblock_patch_comment ... || true` silently ignores a failure to mark the wait comment `done`, so `unblock_latest_wait()` keeps returning a stale open wait on the closed issue.
  WHY: If the issue is then reopened for `/reclarify` as the close comment instructs, a later judge run can reprocess the stale wait and close it again from the same merged fix-up, or produce duplicate API work and a wait record that no longer matches reality (severity disagreement: gemini and luna said MAJOR, minimax and glm said NIT because the pattern copies the #8470 block; anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 rejected it as a pre-existing pattern).
- scripts/unblock_judge.sh:549 | severity=low | confidence=2
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: The jq filter is built by shell interpolation (`'"${fixup}"'`), which is fragile against injection.
  WHY: Not exploitable today because `${fixup}` is validated against `^[1-9][0-9]*$` upstream, so this is defensive only (NIT).
- .github/workflows/unblock_judge.yml:159-183 | severity=low | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5]
  PROBLEM: The "Judge the blocked item" step's env block does not forward UNBLOCK_FIXUP_DELIVERED_CLOSE_ENABLED, so no repository variable can reach the kill switch for the new close path, which is on by default.
  WHY: Operators cannot disable a misfiring close without a code change and a release, unlike the sibling switch that test_unblock_workflow_forwards_nothing_to_implement_close_switch requires (NIT, inherited from the plan; z-ai_glm-5_3-flash rejected it as intended by Implementation step 5 of the issue).
=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
